target: European Sega Master System prototype on PC; preserved original ROM with per-game Export-region emulation

areas.name: Prototype Setup
areas.location_cue: The emulator launch, firmware manager, and first visible hub before any lesson begins.
areas.note: Use the unmodified European prototype and a per-game Export configuration.

save_backup.title: Preserve the untouched prototype
save_backup.why: A compatibility patch changes the build being documented.
save_backup.detail: Keep the E-drive archive unchanged. Work from a verified SSD copy and solve boot failures with the emulator core, region, and legitimate dumped firmware.

levels.1: Confirm the preserved build before changing emulator settings.
levels.2: Hash the extracted Master System ROM and compare it with the known prototype.
levels.3: Use the 262,144-byte European prototype. Its SHA-1 must be f1357505cbcebfab52327a5fc9c3437f54d8da40 and its MD5 must be 5919b101624d4710a10825c34e753ba2; do not patch the ROM to solve a boot problem.

items.label: Supply the Export Master System BIOS

levels.1: A black screen can mean missing firmware.
levels.2: Point the emulator at a valid USA/Europe Master System BIOS dump.
levels.3: For SMSHawk, select the 8,192-byte Export BIOS whose SHA-1 is c315672807d8ddb8d91443729405c766dd95cae7. Keep the firmware outside the game archive and let the emulator identify it as SMS+Export.

levels.1: The prototype's automatic region result is unreliable.
levels.2: Create a per-game Master System region override set to Export.
levels.3: In SMSHawk's sync settings, choose Console Region: Export for this game only. Its database entry requires a BIOS but leaves the region blank, so Auto can choose Japan and produce black video even with valid firmware.

levels.1: Do not accept a successful content load alone.
levels.2: Wait through the BIOS and title, then enter the isometric outdoor map.
levels.3: A correct boot shows the Sega BIOS, the Edusoft title, and then the playable green-island hub after pressing Button 1 at the title. If the frame stays black, stop and correct the core, region, or firmware before playing.

items.label: Keep PicoDrive as the Alternate Core

levels.1: There is a second proven route for this build.
levels.2: Use PicoDrive if the configured SMSHawk route is unavailable.
levels.3: PicoDrive boots the unchanged prototype without the black-frame behavior observed locally in Genesis Plus GX. Preserve the same ROM hash, use native 4:3 output, and test audio and controls before beginning a completion session.

items.label: Create a Clean Hub Save State

levels.1: This unfinished build can misread valid input.
levels.2: Make a state after the hub becomes controllable and before clearing a marker.
levels.3: Save once on the untouched hub, then use separate rolling states during difficult races. Never replace the clean state with a failed reaction prompt or a two-player test; several prototype bugs can make an otherwise valid attempt unwinnable.

areas.name: Question-Mark Options
areas.location_cue: The yellow question mark in the opening green clearing.
areas.note: Inspect every setting before committing to the one-session route.

save_backup.title: Save before the maximal run
save_backup.why: Changing player count or difficulty divides the completion attempt.
save_backup.detail: Create a fresh hub state after choosing Players 1, Complex, Sonic speed, and 4-Way control; keep two-player testing on another state.

point_of_no_return.title: Leaving the menu starts the tracked run
point_of_no_return.why: Progress earned under another option set does not prove the maximal route.
point_of_no_return.detail: Confirm every value before selecting Start. If a value is wrong, return immediately and restart from the clean hub state.

levels.1: Test movement before entering a lesson.
levels.2: Use the D-pad on the hub and Button 1 while standing on a landmark.
levels.3: Move with the D-pad, press Button 1 to enter a map marker, use Button 2 to confirm menu selections, and press both buttons together when a menu refuses to advance with either button alone.

levels.1: One menu choice changes who takes turns.
levels.2: Open the yellow question-mark menu and cycle Players through 1 and 2.
levels.3: Record both settings, then return to Players: 1 before any single-session clear. Two-player mode alternates participants and can invalidate tracking for a one-player all-marker run.

levels.1: Personalize the two three-character slots.
levels.2: Visit Player 1 and Player 2 in the question-mark menu.
levels.3: Enter three initials in each field and confirm them. Player 2 remains configurable even when the current run uses one player, so inspect both fields before leaving the menu.

levels.1: One three-letter entry has an extra reaction.
levels.2: Experiment in the Player 1 initials field.
levels.3: Set Player 1 to DAM and confirm it. This deliberately incomplete spelling triggers the prototype's hidden initials response; restore your preferred initials afterward.

levels.1: The challenge menu has five steps.
levels.2: Cycle Level through Simple, Easy, Medium, Hard, and Complex.
levels.3: Confirm that all five values appear. Difficulty changes word length and the star requirements for transport, so finish the menu audit before choosing the setting for a full run.

levels.1: Mistake tolerance is separately adjustable.
levels.2: Cycle Guesses through Ten, Seven, Five, Three, and One.
levels.3: Inspect all five allowances, then select the value wanted for the run. This option governs the permitted selection attempts and is independent of the race speed and learning level.

levels.1: The timer has five named settings.
levels.2: Cycle Speed through Snail, Tortoise, Hare, Leopard, and Sonic.
levels.3: Check all five values. Snail provides the widest response window; Sonic provides the shortest. Use Snail while mapping content, then return for the dedicated Sonic-speed clear.

levels.1: One input style accepts diagonals directly.
levels.2: Choose Control: Standard and open a word lesson.
levels.3: Move the selection cursor to each of the eight surrounding letter positions with direct D-pad directions, including diagonals. Confirm one harmless answer, then leave or reload before testing the other style.

levels.1: The alternate style avoids diagonal presses.
levels.2: Choose Control: 4-Way and open a word lesson.
levels.3: Reach corner letters by pressing cardinal directions in sequence instead of attempting a diagonal. This is usually the more dependable choice for long words at Sonic speed.

levels.1: Set the demanding run before earning progress.
levels.2: Return to the question mark immediately before the all-marker attempt.
levels.3: For the maximal route, select Players: 1, Level: Complex, Speed: Sonic, Control: 4-Way, and the guess allowance you can manage. Leave these values unchanged until every educational marker has been cleared.

areas.name: Educational Markers
areas.location_cue: Chalkboards and themed object icons distributed across the green islands.
areas.note: Each of the eight lesson types appears twice, for sixteen markers total.

levels.1: Watch both racers after the first prompt.
levels.2: Correct responses move your runner; mistakes or timeouts move the opponent.
levels.3: Earn seven correct responses before the opponent receives seven advances. A timeout behaves like a wrong answer, and losing the race restarts that marker without removing previously banked stars.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable plus-sign chalkboards across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first plus-sign chalkboards when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; solve each displayed sum until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable minus-sign chalkboards across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first minus-sign chalkboards when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; solve each displayed difference until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable multiplication-sign chalkboards across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first multiplication-sign chalkboards when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; solve each displayed product until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable division-sign chalkboards across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first division-sign chalkboards when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; solve each displayed quotient until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable boat icons across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first boat icons when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; spell transport and travel words until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable animal-face icons across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first animal-face icons when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; spell animal names until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable ball icons across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first ball icons when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; spell sport and activity words until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Revisit this symbol whenever another island opens.
levels.2: Enter both reachable picnic icons across the hub.
levels.3: Clear the first picnic icons when it becomes available, then clear its later twin after transport opens the remote islands; spell food and kitchen words until Sonic reaches seven correct advances at each marker.

levels.1: Some word races briefly interrupt the spelling board.
levels.2: Watch for a rapidly changing letter set and its matching instruction.
levels.3: Press the confirm button only when the current set contains the requested matching pair. If the needed pattern never appears, treat the prompt as a prototype failure and reload the rolling state rather than guessing repeatedly.

levels.1: Math races also contain a rapid recognition check.
levels.2: Read the requested factor before the number groups begin cycling.
levels.3: Press confirm only on a displayed group whose values satisfy the requested multiple rule. If a correct set is rejected or no valid set cycles in, reload the pre-lesson state and repeat the marker.

areas.name: Island and Transport Route
areas.location_cue: The connected islands, gates, two helicopters, and striped hot-air balloon.
areas.note: Visit each newly reachable lesson cluster before testing the next barrier.

save_backup.title: Keep one state per unlock wave
save_backup.why: Prototype reaction prompts can reject correct play.
save_backup.detail: Save after the 3, 5, 8, 12, 14, and 16-marker milestones. If a prompt becomes impossible, reload the latest clean wave rather than altering the ROM.

point_of_no_return.title: The completion message ends the route
point_of_no_return.why: The final star check leaves the active hub session.
point_of_no_return.detail: Finish the optional counter and skill-game work first, or retain a state before crossing the difficulty-specific completion threshold.

levels.1: Begin around the question-mark clearing.
levels.2: Enter every educational icon reachable before using transport.
levels.3: Play all three starting markers at least once and repeat comfortable ones until the first helicopter's threshold is met. On Simple this means four stars; higher levels require 8, 12, 16, or 20.

levels.1: A nearby aircraft opens the first detached island.
levels.2: Return to the first helicopter after visiting all three opening markers.
levels.3: Board it with the required stars: 4 on Simple, 8 on Easy, 12 on Medium, 16 on Hard, or 20 on Complex. Clear both educational icons on the island it reaches.

levels.1: The next bridge checks visited lessons.
levels.2: Play both markers beyond the first helicopter, then return to the blocked path.
levels.3: The gate opens after every currently exposed educational location in that branch has been visited. Cross it and play the three new markers, bringing the reachable total from five to eight.

levels.1: Another barrier yields to broader exploration.
levels.2: Visit all three markers beyond the first gate, then backtrack to the lower route.
levels.3: Once the eight-marker wave has been visited, pass the newly opened lower gate and play all four educational markers in the next section. The reachable total is now twelve.

levels.1: The striped balloon needs both exploration and stars.
levels.2: After the twelve-marker wave, build the required star total and return to the balloon.
levels.3: Board with 14 stars on Simple, 28 on Easy, 42 on Medium, 56 on Hard, or 70 on Complex. Play the two markers at its destination, raising the visited total to fourteen.

levels.1: One aircraft passed earlier becomes useful late.
levels.2: After both balloon-side markers, backtrack to the remaining helicopter.
levels.3: Board with 17 stars on Simple, 34 on Easy, 51 on Medium, 68 on Hard, or 85 on Complex. Its destination contains the final two educational markers, for sixteen total.

levels.1: Finish the isolated pair reached by the late helicopter.
levels.2: Enter both educational icons at the aircraft's destination.
levels.3: Win both races and confirm that every earlier marker has also been cleared during this session. If the completion screen does not appear, repeat a quick known marker to build the remaining stars.

levels.1: Clearing all locations and filling the counter are separate checks.
levels.2: Repeat any reliable lesson after all sixteen markers have been visited.
levels.3: Reach 27 stars on Simple, 54 on Easy, 81 on Medium, 108 on Hard, or 135 on Complex. With every educational marker visited, the prototype then displays its completion message.

areas.name: Coffee-Break Games
areas.location_cue: The three balloon-cluster landmarks away from the chalkboards.
areas.note: These one-minute skill games are separate from star progression.

levels.1: Look for one of the balloon-cluster markers.
levels.2: Enter the half-pipe game and target coloured balloons.
levels.3: Send Sonic across when a red or blue balloon is aligned; each is worth 100 points. Avoid grey balloons because touching one ends the attempt. Reach at least 300 points and, for a full survival, continue until the one-minute timer expires.

levels.1: A second balloon marker uses a movable catcher.
levels.2: Keep the trampoline beneath Sonic as he crosses the screen.
levels.3: Hold near the centre until the jump direction is clear, then slide under the landing point. Each successful bounce scores 100; touching the floor ends the run. Survive the full one-minute timer.

levels.1: The remaining balloon marker starts an automatic run.
levels.2: Use both action buttons to test the short and long jumps.
levels.3: Jump over every ground obstacle and collect at least one red or blue balloon for a positive score. Use the smaller hop for close debris and the longer leap for broad gaps; any collision ends the attempt, so survive to the one-minute limit for a clean clear.

levels.1: The skill games do not open transport.
levels.2: Find all three balloon clusters while traversing the hub.
levels.3: Record a completed Balloon Pop, Trampoline, and running-game attempt. They award no progression stars, so do them separately from the educational route and reload if a prototype bug ends a run without your input.

areas.name: Completion and Mastery
areas.location_cue: The fully opened hub after all vehicles and gates are usable.
areas.note: Keep maximal difficulty, counter, and two-player work on deliberately separated states.

save_backup.title: Fork the completed hub state
save_backup.why: Counter farming and two-player mode serve different completion checks.
save_backup.detail: Preserve one pre-ending state, duplicate it for the 255-star farm, and create a third branch before enabling two players.

point_of_no_return.title: Two-player mode breaks the one-player chain
point_of_no_return.why: The maximal single-session route must remain under one participant setting.
point_of_no_return.detail: Do not enable Players 2 until the all-sixteen Complex-and-Sonic run is complete and safely stored.

items.label: Clear All Sixteen in One Session

levels.1: Do not switch player mode midway.
levels.2: Start from the opening hub and win every educational marker without resetting progress.
levels.3: Keep Players set to 1, clear both copies of every math operation and every word theme, and use all three transports as they unlock. Maintain a rolling save state, but do not load a state from another option set.

items.label: Clear Everything on Complex at Sonic Speed

levels.1: Reserve the hardest option pair for a dedicated run.
levels.2: Set Level to Complex and Speed to Sonic before clearing any marker.
levels.3: Use 4-Way control, keep Players at 1, and clear all sixteen educational markers without changing either difficulty setting. Build to 135 stars if the completion screen has not appeared after the final marker.

levels.1: Choose a lesson whose answers you know instantly.
levels.2: At Sonic speed, finish one race before the opponent advances.
levels.3: Use a short math lesson or a memorized word group, answer seven prompts correctly, and avoid every timeout or wrong selection. Reload immediately if the opponent moves even once.

levels.1: Fast recognition can end a race unusually early.
levels.2: Select Sonic speed and choose a familiar marker.
levels.3: Answer each prompt as soon as it settles and earn the seventh correct response before the urgent countdown music begins. A Simple math board is the safest rehearsal; repeat on Complex for the maximal version.

levels.1: The counter continues beyond the ending threshold.
levels.2: Repeat a reliable educational marker after transport is fully open.
levels.3: Keep winning the fastest comfortable lesson until the total reaches 100. Coffee-break games do not add stars, so use a short math board or a memorized three-letter word bank for the repeat cycle.

levels.1: The prototype stores more than completion requires.
levels.2: Continue repeating educational wins after reaching 100.
levels.3: Raise the counter to its 255 maximum by farming the quickest dependable marker. Make a separate save state first: this is a counter-cap exercise, not a requirement for the normal completion screen.

levels.1: The second participant setting deserves its own test.
levels.2: Set Players to 2 only after finishing the one-player mastery run.
levels.3: Give both participants initials, enter an opening marker, and complete enough turns to observe the handoff. Save this as a separate branch, because enabling two-player mode breaks continuity with the single-session one-player clear.
